# PSP Consultancy: full reference

Last updated 2026-10-06. Business & Financial Advisory. Ahmedabad, India. Source: https://www.pspconsultancy.com/

## Income Tax Advisory and Return Filing
URL: https://www.pspconsultancy.com/services/income-tax/

PSP Consultancy helps individuals, professionals, HUFs, firms and companies file accurate income tax returns, plan tax legally, manage advance tax and TDS, and respond to departmental notices. Tax audit reports and other certificates that the law reserves for Chartered Accountants are issued by our affiliate firm, PSP & Associates.

- Return filing: Returns for salaried individuals, business and professional income, capital gains, rental income, foreign income and assets, HUFs, firms, LLPs and companies, reconciled with the Annual Information Statement and tax credit statements before filing.
- Tax planning and regime choice: Old versus new regime comparison for individuals and HUFs, deduction and investment planning, and structuring advice for business owners and professionals.
- Advance tax, TDS and TCS: Advance tax computation and payment, review of TDS and TCS deduction and deposit, and preparation of statements so that interest and late fees are avoided.
- Notices and assessments: Review of intimations, mismatch and defective-return notices, scrutiny and rectification requests, with drafted responses and a documentation trail. Appearance before authorities is handled through an authorised representative, as the Act permits.
- Capital gains and ESOPs: Tax on the sale of property, shares, mutual funds and employee stock options, including holding periods, exemptions and reinvestment timelines.
- NRI and cross-border income: Residential status, taxation of Indian income, treaty (DTAA) relief, tax on property sales by non-residents and disclosure of foreign assets.
- Refunds and credit reconciliation: Tracking pending refunds, correcting TDS credit mismatches and following up with deductors.
- Tax audit coordination: We prepare the books and schedules and manage the process. The audit report itself is signed by a practising CA at PSP & Associates.

Key facts:
- Law for income up to 31 March 2026: Income-tax Act, 1961 (FY 2025-26, assessed in AY 2026-27)
- Law from 1 April 2026: Income-tax Act, 2025, which replaces the 1961 Act and uses a single "tax year"
- Default regime for individuals: New regime, unless you opt for the old one

FAQ:
Q: Which law applies to my return this year?
A: Income earned up to 31 March 2026 (FY 2025-26, assessed in AY 2026-27) remains under the Income-tax Act, 1961. Income earned from 1 April 2026 falls under the Income-tax Act, 2025, which uses a single "tax year" instead of previous year and assessment year.

Q: Who needs to file an income tax return?
A: Anyone whose total income exceeds the basic exemption limit under the regime they follow must file. Some people must file even below that limit, for example when they hold foreign assets, make large deposits or expenditure above specified thresholds, or want to claim a refund. We confirm this from your documents.

Q: Should I choose the old or the new tax regime?
A: The new regime is the default for individuals and HUFs and the old regime applies only if you opt for it. The better choice depends on your deductions and exemptions, so we compute both before filing.

Q: What should I do if I receive an income tax notice?
A: Do not ignore it. Note the section, the date and the response deadline, and send us the notice with supporting documents. We review it, prepare the reply and track it to closure.

Q: Can NRIs file their Indian returns through you from abroad?
A: Yes. Documents are shared digitally, and we handle residential status, treaty relief and disclosures. If a matter needs a Chartered Accountant's certificate, PSP & Associates issues it.

Q: Who signs a tax audit report?
A: A tax audit report can only be signed by a practising Chartered Accountant. That is done by PSP & Associates, our separate affiliate CA firm. PSP Consultancy supports with books, schedules and coordination.

## GST Registration, Returns and Advisory
URL: https://www.pspconsultancy.com/services/gst/

PSP Consultancy handles GST registration, monthly and annual return filing, input tax credit reconciliation, e-invoicing and e-way bill advice, refunds and replies to notices for businesses in Gujarat and across India. We work from your books and keep the filing calendar so nothing is missed.

- Registration and amendments: New registration, voluntary registration, composition scheme eligibility, changes to business details and cancellation, with the supporting documents prepared in advance.
- Return filing: GSTR-1 or IFF, GSTR-3B and the annual return where applicable, prepared from your sales and purchase records and filed on time.
- Input tax credit reconciliation: Books matched with GSTR-2B, vendor follow-up on missing invoices, identification of ineligible or reversible credit, and a monthly reconciliation you can audit.
- E-invoicing and e-way bills: Applicability checks, process set-up for your accounting software, and help resolving rejections and errors.
- Refunds: Export refunds under a Letter of Undertaking or on payment of IGST, inverted-duty refunds and excess cash-ledger balances, with the reconciliation the department expects.
- Notices, assessments and appeals: Replies to show-cause notices and assessment orders, and appeal drafting. Representation is through an authorised representative as the GST law permits.
- GST health check and due diligence: A structured review before fundraising, a sale or a statutory audit, covering ITC, rate classification, place of supply and compliance history.
- Classification and rate advice: HSN classification, place-of-supply questions and the impact of rate changes, including the September 2025 rate rationalisation.

Key facts:
- Registration threshold (goods): ₹40 lakh aggregate turnover (lower for special-category states), unless compulsory registration applies
- Registration threshold (services): ₹20 lakh aggregate turnover (lower for special-category states)
- Monthly return due dates: GSTR-1 by the 11th and GSTR-3B by the 20th of the following month, for monthly filers
- Main rate slabs since 22 September 2025: 5%, 18% and 40%, with 0% and special rates for specified goods

FAQ:
Q: Do I need GST registration?
A: You must register once your aggregate turnover crosses ₹40 lakh for goods or ₹20 lakh for services (lower limits apply in special-category states). Registration is compulsory regardless of turnover in certain cases, such as e-commerce supply and some inter-state supplies. Many smaller businesses register voluntarily to claim input tax credit.

Q: When are GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B due?
A: For monthly filers, GSTR-1 is due by the 11th and GSTR-3B by the 20th of the following month. Dates differ for taxpayers under the quarterly scheme and are sometimes extended by notification, so we track the current calendar.

Q: What is input tax credit and how do I avoid losing it?
A: Input tax credit lets you set off GST paid on business purchases against GST payable on sales. To claim it you need a valid tax invoice, receipt of the goods or services, the tax paid by your supplier and the return filed, within the time limit. Regular reconciliation with GSTR-2B is the best protection.

Q: What happens if I miss a GST return?
A: A late fee and interest on unpaid tax apply, and continued non-filing can lead to cancellation of registration and restrictions on e-way bills. File as soon as possible and speak to us about the cleanest way to regularise.

Q: What are the current GST rates?
A: Since 22 September 2025 most goods and services fall under 5% or 18%, with 40% on specified goods and 0% or special rates for certain items. We confirm the rate and classification for your product or service before you invoice.

Q: Can you represent us in a GST notice or appeal?
A: Yes, through an authorised representative as permitted under the GST law. Where a matter needs a certificate that only a Chartered Accountant can give, PSP & Associates issues it.

## RERA Registration and Compliance Advisory
URL: https://www.pspconsultancy.com/services/rera-advisory/

PSP Consultancy supports developers, promoters and real estate agents with RERA project registration, periodic project updates, annual filings, escrow-account compliance and compliance reviews, so projects stay within the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 and the rules of the state authority, including Gujarat RERA.

- Project registration and extension: Preparing the application, project details, disclosures and supporting documents for registration, and managing extension requests when timelines move.
- Periodic updates and annual filings: Regular project progress updates and annual financial filings in the format the state authority prescribes, so the project page shows current, consistent data.
- Escrow account and withdrawals: RERA requires that 70% of money received from buyers is kept in a separate designated account, with withdrawals linked to project progress. We set up the tracking, and the practising CA certificate is issued through PSP & Associates.
- RERA compliance health check: A review of registration status, disclosures, agreements, fund flow and filings, with a prioritised list of gaps before a complaint or inspection finds them.
- Agent registration and renewal: Registration and renewal for real estate agents, and guidance on the conduct rules that apply to them.
- Complaint and notice response: Reviewing complaints and notices, collating project records and drafting the factual response, in coordination with your legal counsel.
- Project-wise tax support: GST on construction and sale, income tax on project profits and joint development arrangements, linked to the RERA numbers so the two never disagree.
- Project financial reporting: Cost-to-complete, collections versus construction progress and fund tracking, delivered as a monthly report for promoters and lenders.

Key facts:
- Projects that must register: Land above 500 sq m or more than 8 apartments (all phases included)
- Buyer money to be held in escrow: 70% of amounts realised from allottees
- Authority for Gujarat projects: Gujarat Real Estate Regulatory Authority (Gujarat RERA)

FAQ:
Q: Which projects need RERA registration?
A: A project must be registered if the land proposed to be developed exceeds 500 square metres or the number of apartments exceeds eight, counting all phases. Projects that had not received a completion certificate when the Act came into force are also covered as ongoing projects.

Q: What is the 70% escrow rule?
A: Under the Act, 70% of the amounts realised from buyers for a project must be deposited in a separate designated bank account and used only for the construction cost and land cost of that project. Withdrawals follow certification of project progress.

Q: What filings does a registered project have to make?
A: State authorities require regular project updates and annual audited financial information in their prescribed formats. Frequency and formats differ by state and change over time, so we confirm the current requirement before each filing.

Q: Can an agent work without RERA registration?
A: No. A real estate agent who facilitates the sale of units in a RERA-registered project must be registered with the authority and quote the registration number in dealings.

Q: Who certifies fund withdrawals from the escrow account?
A: The authority's format requires certification by the project's engineer and architect and by a practising Chartered Accountant. The Chartered Accountant's certificate is issued through PSP & Associates.

Q: What if my project is running late?
A: Delay can expose a promoter to interest payable to buyers and to action by the authority. We help prepare a realistic revised timeline, the extension request where eligible, and the communication to buyers.

## FEMA Advisory: FDI, Overseas Investment, ECB and Export-Import
URL: https://www.pspconsultancy.com/services/fema-advisory/

PSP Consultancy advises Indian businesses, foreign investors and NRIs on the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999: foreign investment reporting, overseas investment, external commercial borrowings, export and import compliance, NRI remittances, and compounding of past contraventions. Where a Chartered Accountant's certificate is required, PSP & Associates issues it.

- FDI inflows: structuring and reporting: Eligibility by sector and entry route, pricing compliance, and the reporting that follows an allotment or transfer of shares, filed through RBI's reporting portal with your authorised dealer bank.
- Overseas investment: Structuring and reporting for Indian entities and residents investing abroad, including the annual reporting that follows.
- External commercial borrowings: Eligibility, permitted end-use, loan registration and the periodic returns that follow.
- Export-import compliance: Export Declaration Forms, tracking of realisation periods, extension requests and bank liaison under the unified export-import regulations in force from 1 October 2026.
- NRI investments, property and remittances: Account types, investment routes, sale of property, repatriation within the limits and the tax compliance that must accompany it.
- Annual return on foreign liabilities and assets: Preparing and filing the annual return that companies with foreign investment must submit to RBI.
- Compounding and regularisation: Assessing late or missed filings, preparing the application to RBI and presenting facts clearly, with the late submission fee where it applies.
- Remittance certification support: Preparing the information for foreign remittances. The Chartered Accountant's certificate that some remittances require is issued through PSP & Associates.

Key facts:
- Share allotment to a foreign investor: Reported on Form FC-GPR, typically within 30 days of allotment
- Transfer of shares involving a non-resident: Reported on Form FC-TRS, typically within 60 days of transfer
- Annual FLA return: Typically due by 15 July each year
- Export realisation (from 1 October 2026): Generally 9 months, or 12 months for exports invoiced or settled in rupees

FAQ:
Q: What is FEMA and who does it affect?
A: The Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 regulates foreign exchange transactions in India. It affects companies receiving or making foreign investment, exporters and importers, borrowers from overseas lenders, and individuals who hold or move money across borders, including NRIs.

Q: What are the timelines for reporting foreign investment?
A: Reporting of an allotment of shares to a foreign investor is typically required within 30 days, and reporting of a transfer of shares typically within 60 days. RBI revises these requirements from time to time, so we confirm the current rule before filing.

Q: What changed for exporters from 1 October 2026?
A: A unified set of export-import regulations took effect on 1 October 2026, with a 9-month period to realise export proceeds in most cases. Our article on the new regulations explains the changes and gives a checklist.

Q: What is compounding under FEMA?
A: Compounding is a process under which RBI can settle a contravention on application, usually for a monetary payment, without a prosecution. It is used for late filings and other procedural breaches, and a clean, early application helps.

Q: Can NRIs repatriate the sale proceeds of property in India?
A: Yes, within the limits and conditions that apply to the type of account and the property, and subject to tax being paid and certified. Currently NRO balances can generally be repatriated up to USD 1 million per financial year. We confirm the current position for your case.

Q: Do you handle applications to RBI?
A: Most requests go through your authorised dealer bank. We prepare the application, the explanation and the supporting documents, and coordinate with the bank. Certificates that must come from a Chartered Accountant are issued through PSP & Associates.

## Audit and Assurance, through PSP & Associates
URL: https://www.pspconsultancy.com/services/audit-assurance/

Statutory audit, tax audit, internal audit, RERA audit and forensic or management reviews are carried out by PSP & Associates, our separate affiliate Chartered Accountancy firm registered with the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. PSP Consultancy coordinates the engagement. Audit reports are signed only by PSP & Associates.

- Statutory audit: Audit of companies and LLPs as required by the Companies Act, 2013 and the LLP Act, 2008.
- Tax audit: Audit of the books of businesses and professionals whose turnover or receipts exceed the prescribed limits, with the report filed in the form the tax law requires.
- Internal audit: Risk-based review of processes, controls and compliance, with a written report and recommendations for management.
- RERA audit: Annual audit and certification for real estate projects registered under RERA, in the authority's format.
- Forensic and fraud review: Fact-finding on suspected irregularities, with documentation suitable for management, lenders or counsel.
- Management and process audit: Review of operating processes, cost controls and reporting quality, with practical improvement steps.
- Financial due diligence support: Reviewing financial statements and compliance history for investors, buyers and lenders.

Key facts:
- Who signs audit reports: A practising Chartered Accountant at PSP & Associates, never PSP Consultancy
- Regulator of the audit firm: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI)

FAQ:
Q: Who signs the audit report?
A: Only PSP & Associates. It is a Chartered Accountancy firm registered with ICAI. PSP Consultancy is not an audit firm and does not sign audit reports or certificates.

Q: Is PSP Consultancy an audit firm?
A: No. PSP Consultancy is a separate advisory practice. It helps you scope the work, gather documents and follow up, while the audit itself is performed by PSP & Associates.

Q: Can the same group audit us and also advise us?
A: Independence rules under the Companies Act and ICAI's Code of Ethics restrict certain other services to an audit client. We assess this at the start of every engagement and structure who does what accordingly.

Q: What is a tax audit and who needs one?
A: A tax audit is an audit of the books of a business or professional whose turnover or receipts exceed the limits prescribed in the tax law, or who is otherwise covered. We confirm the thresholds for your facts before the due date.

Q: How do we get started?
A: Contact us with a short description of the entity and the year. We confirm the scope and arrange for PSP & Associates to share its engagement terms.

## Virtual CFO Services
URL: https://www.pspconsultancy.com/services/virtual-cfo/

A Virtual CFO gives a growing business senior finance leadership on a monthly retainer: reliable MIS, budgets and forecasts, cash-flow control, fundraising readiness and a point of contact for lenders, investors and auditors. PSP Consultancy provides this alongside the tax, GST and FEMA expertise that most finance heads have to chase separately.

- Monthly MIS and dashboards: A consistent monthly pack covering profit and loss, balance sheet, cash and the three or four numbers that run your business, delivered by a fixed working day.
- Budgeting and forecasting: Annual budgets, rolling forecasts and scenario views that show what a hire, a price change or a delayed collection does to cash.
- Cash-flow and working-capital management: Receivables and payables discipline, collection follow-up, inventory cover and a 13-week cash view where it is needed.
- Unit economics and pricing: Margin by product, customer or project, and pricing and discount guardrails based on actual cost.
- Fundraising and lender readiness: Financial models, investor reporting, a clean data room and answers to diligence questions, including tax, GST and FEMA readiness.
- Board and investor reporting: Monthly or quarterly packs in a format investors recognise, with variance commentary.
- Controls and finance processes: Approval limits, month-end close routines, document trails and simple SOPs that survive staff changes.
- Compliance calendar oversight: A single calendar of tax, GST, payroll and regulatory dates, owned by someone, with reminders before each deadline.

Key facts:
- Bookkeeper: Records transactions accurately; usually does not advise on decisions
- Virtual CFO: Turns the records into decisions, forecasts and funding readiness, on a monthly retainer
- Full-time CFO: Embedded leadership, usually justified at larger scale or complexity

FAQ:
Q: What is a Virtual CFO?
A: A Virtual CFO, also called a fractional or outsourced CFO, is an experienced finance professional who provides CFO-level support part-time, usually on a monthly retainer, instead of an in-house full-time hire.

Q: How is a Virtual CFO different from an accountant?
A: An accountant records and reports what happened and files returns. A Virtual CFO uses that information to plan: budgets, forecasts, cash management, pricing, fundraising and board reporting.

Q: When should a business consider a Virtual CFO?
A: Typical triggers are preparing to raise capital, cash tightness despite profits, multiple entities or locations, lender or investor reporting requirements, and an owner who spends too much time on finance.

Q: How is the fee decided?
A: By scope: size of the business, number of entities, reporting frequency and the level of involvement. We quote a fixed monthly fee in writing before any work begins.

Q: Do you work with our existing accountant and software?
A: Yes. We work in your existing accounting software and with your current team, and improve processes gradually instead of replacing everything at once.

## Accounting, Bookkeeping and Payroll Outsourcing
URL: https://www.pspconsultancy.com/services/outsourcing/

PSP Consultancy runs the finance back office for businesses that would rather not: bookkeeping, accounts payable and receivable, bank reconciliation, payroll with statutory deductions and filings, and a monthly MIS. Books stay GST-ready and audit-ready, and tax and compliance questions are answered by the same team.

- Bookkeeping: Day-to-day recording of sales, purchases, expenses and bank transactions, maintained in your accounting software and closed monthly.
- Accounts payable and receivable: Vendor bill processing and payment scheduling, customer invoicing and collection follow-up, with ageing reports.
- Bank and ledger reconciliation: Monthly reconciliation of bank, vendor, customer and GST ledgers, with exceptions listed and resolved.
- Payroll processing: Salary computation, payslips, and the statutory side: provident fund, ESI, professional tax, TDS on salary and labour welfare fund where they apply.
- MIS and management reporting: A monthly pack with profit and loss, balance sheet, cash position, budget versus actual and a short commentary.
- Month-end and year-end close: Accruals, depreciation, provisions and the schedules your auditor will ask for, prepared on a fixed timetable.
- Digital payments accounting: Correct treatment of payment-gateway and UPI merchant charges, settlements net of fees and the GST on those charges.

Key facts:
- Provident fund wage ceiling: ₹25,000 per month from 17 September 2026, up from ₹15,000
- ESI wage ceiling: ₹21,000 per month (unchanged by the PF notification)
- UPI merchant charges: 0.4% on eligible payments above ₹2,000 from 15 October 2026, capped at ₹300

FAQ:
Q: What does accounting outsourcing include?
A: It typically covers bookkeeping, payables and receivables, reconciliations, payroll, month-end close and a monthly MIS. We agree the exact scope and the calendar in writing.

Q: Can you work in our existing accounting software?
A: Yes. We work in the software you already use, and discuss changes only if something is clearly holding you back.

Q: How does payroll outsourcing handle statutory compliance?
A: We compute salaries, deductions and employer contributions, prepare payslips and the statutory returns and challans, and keep a calendar of due dates. Recent changes such as the new provident fund wage ceiling are built into the payroll set-up.

Q: Is our financial data safe?
A: We restrict access to named people, use your software's access controls, and handle personal data in line with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. Details are in our privacy policy.

Q: What if we want to bring accounting back in-house?
A: Your books stay in your software and you keep the data. We hand over the working papers and the calendar so a new team can take over without a gap.

## India Business Entry: Set-up, Structuring and Compliance
URL: https://www.pspconsultancy.com/services/india-business-entry/

PSP Consultancy helps foreign companies and founders enter India: choosing between a private limited company, LLP, subsidiary or branch, completing incorporation and registrations, reporting the foreign investment to RBI, and putting first-year tax, GST and ROC compliance in place.

- Entity selection and structuring: Comparison of a private limited company, LLP, wholly owned subsidiary, branch, liaison or project office against your sector, funding, tax and exit plans.
- Incorporation and registrations: Name approval, incorporation, PAN and TAN, GST, bank account opening, and registrations specific to your activity.
- FDI structuring and reporting: Sector and entry-route checks, pricing compliance, share issue and the RBI reporting that follows.
- Startup India recognition: Eligibility review and DPIIT recognition application for qualifying startups.
- Tax and transfer pricing set-up: Understanding how the Indian entity will be taxed, intercompany agreements and documentation where related-party transactions arise.
- Accounting, payroll and compliance: Opening books, first auditor appointment, payroll registrations and the annual ROC and tax calendar.
- Banking and funding support: Introductions and documentation for bank accounts, foreign inward remittance and capital infusion.
- Exit and restructuring support: Share transfers, mergers, closure or conversion, with the FEMA and tax steps they involve.

Key facts:
- Private limited company: Minimum two directors and two shareholders, with at least one director resident in India
- LLP: Minimum two partners, with at least one designated partner resident in India
- Branch or liaison office: Requires approval through an authorised dealer bank or RBI, with restricted activities
- Wholly owned subsidiary: A private limited company held by the foreign parent, where the sector permits 100% FDI

FAQ:
Q: Which entity should a foreign company choose in India?
A: Most foreign investors use a private limited company, usually a wholly owned subsidiary, because it is straightforward for investment and exit. An LLP suits some professional and service businesses, while branch and liaison offices need approvals and have limited permitted activities. The right choice depends on the sector, funding and tax position.

Q: Is a resident director mandatory?
A: Yes. A company must have at least one director who has stayed in India for at least 182 days during the year, as the Companies Act specifies, and an LLP must have at least one designated partner resident in India.

Q: How long does incorporation take?
A: Incorporation itself can be quick when documents are ready. Overall timelines depend on name approval, apostille or notarisation of foreign documents, and bank account opening, so we plan the whole sequence with you.

Q: What must be reported to RBI after receiving foreign investment?
A: The allotment of shares to the foreign investor is reported through RBI's portal, typically within 30 days of allotment, and the company later files an annual return on foreign liabilities and assets. We handle both.

Q: Can an NRI or foreign national start a company in India?
A: Yes, subject to the sector rules and the FDI policy. Foreign nationals can be directors or shareholders, and we help with documents, the resident director requirement and registrations.

## UPI MDR 2026: 0.4% Charge from 15 October Explained
URL: https://www.pspconsultancy.com/insights/upi-mdr-2026-15-october/ (published 2026-10-06)

From 15 October 2026, merchants pay a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) of 0.4% on eligible person-to-merchant UPI payments above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 per transaction. The cap starts to apply at ₹75,000. Customers are not charged, payments up to ₹2,000 stay free, and small merchants are exempt.

FAQ:
Q: Will customers be charged for UPI payments from 15 October 2026?
A: No. MDR is a merchant-side charge. Person-to-person transfers and merchant payments up to ₹2,000 remain free, and UPI apps cannot add a platform fee.

Q: What is the UPI MDR rate?
A: A 0.4% MDR applies to eligible person-to-merchant payments above ₹2,000. It is capped at ₹300 per transaction for payments of ₹75,000 and above.

Q: Who is exempt from UPI MDR?
A: Payments up to ₹2,000, person-to-person transfers, UPI AutoPay mandates, and small merchants receiving up to ₹1 lakh a month through UPI QR codes fall outside the 0.4% rate.

Q: Which payments have a different MDR?
A: A flat ₹5 applies above ₹2,000 for sectors such as railways, telecom, insurance, fuel, agricultural inputs and utility bills. Payments for mutual funds, securities and stockbrokers carry 0.02%, capped at ₹300.

Q: Can a merchant pass the MDR on to the customer?
A: No. Banks have been advised to ensure merchants do not pass MDR on, so a separate UPI charge on the bill is not allowed.

Q: Is GST charged on UPI MDR?
A: GST is reported to apply at 18% on MDR, and eligible GST-registered merchants can claim input tax credit. Confirm the rate on your acquiring bank's invoice.

## EPF Wage Ceiling ₹25,000 (2026): Employer Checklist
URL: https://www.pspconsultancy.com/insights/epf-wage-ceiling-25000-2026/ (published 2026-10-06)

The monthly wage ceiling for provident fund coverage rose from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 with effect from 17 September 2026, by notification S.O. 5109(E). Employees earning between ₹15,001 and ₹25,000 who were outside mandatory coverage can now come within it, and continuing members can contribute on a higher base. The September return and payment are due by 15 October 2026.

FAQ:
Q: What is the new EPF wage ceiling?
A: ₹25,000 a month from 17 September 2026, up from ₹15,000, which had applied since September 2014.

Q: Does the new ceiling apply from 17 October?
A: No. It applies from 17 September 2026. The September return and payment are due by 15 October 2026, and October is the first full wage month at the new ceiling.

Q: Who is now covered?
A: Employees earning between ₹15,001 and ₹25,000 a month become eligible for mandatory EPF, EPS and EDLI coverage, subject to the applicable provisions.

Q: How much more will an employee and employer pay?
A: Where contribution was restricted to ₹15,000, the employee share rises by up to ₹1,200 a month at the full ceiling. The employer's matching share rises by the same amount.

Q: How should September 2026 be handled?
A: Because the change took effect mid-month, one reading is a split month: 1 to 16 September on ₹15,000 and 17 to 30 September on ₹25,000. Commentary differs on how the return portal handles this, so confirm EPFO's instructions before filing.

## FEMA Export-Import Regulations 2026: What Changed
URL: https://www.pspconsultancy.com/insights/fema-export-import-regulations-2026/ (published 2026-10-06)

The Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026 took effect on 1 October 2026, replacing the 2015 export regulations. After RBI's amendment of 22 September 2026, exporters generally have nine months to realise export proceeds, or twelve months where exports are invoiced or settled in rupees. Service exporters file the Export Declaration Form monthly.

FAQ:
Q: What are the FEMA export-import regulations, 2026?
A: They are the RBI's unified regulations (Notification FEMA 23(R)/2026-RB) covering exports and imports of goods, services and software. They replace the 2015 export regulations and took effect on 1 October 2026.

Q: How long do exporters have to realise export proceeds?
A: Nine months from the date of shipment for goods or the invoice date for services, and twelve months where exports are invoiced or settled in rupees. Banks can extend the period on request, with reasons.

Q: What did the 22 September 2026 amendment change?
A: It cut the realisation periods from 15 to 9 months, and from 18 to 12 months for rupee exports. It also kept Caution List exporters under earlier orders and let banks handle pre-October cases that needed RBI approval.

Q: Are there simpler rules for small transactions?
A: Yes. For shipping bills or invoices up to ₹10 lakh, banks can close monitoring-system entries and allow reduced export value on the exporter's declaration.

Q: When must service exporters file the Export Declaration Form?
A: Within 30 days of the end of the month in which the invoice was raised. One form can cover all of that month's service exports.
